title: Code Reviewer Dynamic Review findings, version 1
description: The neutral findings a Dynamic Review returns (#195), before the trusted runner renders them into the persistent summary comment (#199). The prompt and the publisher consume this shape. It is deliberately opaque and authority-free: opaque stable ids, a P0-P3 priority, a confidence, a bounded title/body, a safe repository-relative path and line range, evidence references, the ids the run resolved, and the exact reviewed SHA. It carries no permission, provider, hosting-provider, routing, endpoint or command field, and no field may add one: the fixed core, the tools and the limits are runner-owned. Fields are bounded so an untrusted model answer cannot grow a comment past the API limit. Existing JobResult/usage stays the completion envelope.

Priority.description: The severity of a finding, highest first. Stable: a caller branches on it.

Finding.description: One neutral finding. `path` is repository-relative and lexically safe (no absolute path, drive, traversal or backslash); ordered line ranges and membership in the verified export are the runner's semantic check (#196/#199). `reviewedSha` is the exact head the finding was made against.

path.description: Repository-relative; no leading slash, no drive letter, no backslash, no `..` segment.

DynamicFindings.description: The versioned output of one Dynamic Review. `schemaVersion` is the version of this file; `reviewedSha` is the exact head the whole run was made against. `resolvedIds` names the findings of earlier runs this run affirmatively reassessed — it lives on the envelope, so a run that leaves no current finding can still report its resolutions. At most maxFindings (1-30) findings.

resolvedIds.description: Ids of findings of earlier runs this run affirmatively reassessed, independently of the current findings. Never a way to resolve by absence.
